svg.text: TEACHER ANCHOR: CCSS.K.OA.A.3 • TEKS 111.3.b.3.A • UNSPSC 60101700 • TITLE I / IV GRANT ELIGIBLE • MODEL: SC6
LESSON GUIDE: TRIANGULAR COMBINATORICS & PART-WHOLE SUMS
Grades K–5 Addition, Part-Whole & Combinatorics • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

g.text: STEP 1: LINE UP DOUBLES SPINE [0|0] TO [6|6]

text.tspan: Place the 7 double tiles in the lid's organizer spine:
These 7 doubles form the diagonal spine of the 28-tile triangle!
Find tiles whose pip sum equals 6: [0|6], [1|5], [2|4], [3|3].
Place them in the 12-frame tray side by side.
Observe the inverse symmetry: as left side increases by 1,
the right side decreases by 1, preserving the constant sum 6!
3. COMBINE TWO TILES: Take tile [5|4] (sum 9) and [3|2] (sum 5). Seat in 12-frame tray.
Calculator Verification: Press Domino Pip Pattern Icon ([g][COUNT] & [g][a:b]) and run 5 [ENTER] 4 [+] 3 [ENTER] 2 [+] [+] → 14.

g.text: THE BIG AHA! THE 28-TILE TRIANGULAR NUMBER SECRET

text.tspan: Why are there exactly 28 tiles? Count them by their highest pip: 7 tiles have a 0 ([0|0]..[0|6]),
6 new tiles have a 1 ([1|1]..[1|6]), 5 have a 2, down to 1 tile with a 6 ([6|6]).
Sum: 7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 28! Dominoes are triangular numbers made tactile!

g.text: ★ NOW YOU TRY! (STUDENT PRACTICE CHALLENGE): FIND ALL SUM-TO-7 TILES

text.tspan: Can you find all 3 tiles that sum to 7: [1|6], [2|5], and [3|4]? Why is there no [0|7] tile in a double-six set? (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Build with your blocks, then scan the QR code to watch the animated 3D solution on your screen!
